rationale: Tests application of receptor pharmacology to predict the baroreceptor reflex response to a selective α1 agonist, anchoring after the block establishing adrenergic receptor families and their physiological effects.
Tests recall of adrenergic drug receptor selectivity and mechanism categories from the classification block.
Tests the ability to select an evidence-based beta-blocker for a patient with concurrent HFrEF and COPD, anchoring after the block covering adrenergic antagonists.
Tests emergency application of adrenaline pharmacology in anaphylaxis — the core clinical scenario of this SDL — anchoring after the block on emergency sympathomimetic use.
Tests understanding of the alpha-first rule in phaeochromocytoma — a high-yield clinical pearl where student misconceptions are common.
Tests understanding of the muscarinic toxidrome resulting from AChE inhibition, the key pathophysiological concept established in this block on cholinergic transmission.
Consolidates recall of cholinergic drug–mechanism–use relationships from the classification block, using paired flip-cards for five key agents.
Tests clinical application of the quaternary vs tertiary amine distinction in choosing an anticholinergic for a patient with COPD and cognitive vulnerability.
Tests the critical clinical decision of atropine titration endpoint in OPC poisoning — the highest-yield emergency concept from this block.
Tests the clinically important distinction between carbamate and organophosphate poisoning management — a genuine point of student uncertainty from this clinical pearl.
Tests understanding of why centrally acting spasmolytics are appropriate for ambulatory spasticity while NMBDs are contraindicated, anchoring after the therapeutic rationale block.
Tests the critical clinical decision of NMBD selection in a patient with contraindications to succinylcholine, the key pharmacokinetic application from this block.
Tests recall of centrally acting muscle relaxant mechanisms and key safety concerns from this block.
Tests recognition and emergency management of malignant hyperthermia, the highest-stakes clinical scenario in muscle relaxant pharmacology.
Tests understanding of sugammadex's mechanism and clinical significance as a reversal agent in failed-airway emergencies — the key concept from this clinical pearl.
Tests the critical pharmacokinetic concept of pH-dependent ionisation and its clinical consequence of LA failure in infected tissue.
Tests recall of the key metabolic and safety distinctions between ester and amide LA classes established in this classification block.
Tests integration of PK determinants (hepatic metabolism, cardiac toxicity, duration) in choosing an LA for a patient with organ impairment.
Tests knowledge of the absolute contraindication of bupivacaine in Bier's block — a life-saving safety rule from the administration techniques block.
Tests understanding of the lipid emulsion rescue mechanism — a critical safety intervention that must be available wherever long-acting amide LAs are administered.
